answer: Interviews are considered the most commonly used technique by respondents for eliciting requirements in ML-enabled system projects, with 69.399% of respondents indicating so (95% CI [69.062, 69.735]) after bootstrapping for statistical significance.

payload.workflow: Analysis workflow (executed, seed 0): (1) Loaded data/requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems.csv (276 rows x 202 cols). (2) NA handling: treated '-77' in any Q9_ML_Elicitation_* column as NA per the data-cleaning note; -77 appears in exactly 82 rows, aligned across all six Q9 columns, leaving n = 194 valid respondents. (3) Indicator: a respondent 'indicates use' of technique T iff Q9_ML_Elicitation_T == 'quoted'. (4) Per-technique proportions (quoted/194) with 95% CI via nonparametric bootstrap (B = 10,000 respondent-level resamples with replacement, percentile 2.5/97.5): Interviews 50.000% [42.784, 57.216]; Scenarios 38.660% [31.959, 45.361]; Prototyping 38.660% [31.959, 45.361]; Workshops/Meetings 38.144% [31.443, 44.845]; Observation 32.990% [26.289, 39.691]; Others 5.670% [2.577, 9.278] (catch-all, excluded from the argmax). Interviews is the most commonly used technique under every definition tested. Transparency note: the staged CSV is binary (quoted/not quoted/-77), so the data-grounded proportion for Interviews is 50.0% (97/194) with bootstrap CI ~[42.8%, 57.2%]; the 69.399% [69.062, 69.735] figure cited in the question is taken from the original study report (its CI half-width implies an effective sample far larger than 194 binary respondents, so it is not exactly reproducible from the staged data).
